slides.heading: Primary Health Care
slides.subtitle: Essential, accessible, affordable health care made universal through full community participation — "Health in the hands of the people."

slides.heading: Definition & Legal Basis
bullets: Essential health care based on practical, scientifically sound, socially acceptable methods, universally accessible at a cost the community can afford (WHO 1978, UNICEF).
Declared at the Alma Ata Conference (Kazakhstan), 1978.
LOI 949 — legal basis of PHC in the Philippines (Marcos, Oct 1979).
Vision: "Health in the hands of the people."
Mission: increase opportunities for people to manage their own health care.

terms.definition: Active collaboration between health workers and the community.
Transfer of knowledge, skills and attitude to the people.

slides.heading: 4 Pillars of PHC
bullets: Active community participation — the MOST important pillar.
Intra- & inter-sectoral linkages (intra = within the health system; inter = NGOs, government).
Use of appropriate technology (local indigenous resources, e.g., herbal).
Support mechanism made available (support from the local government).

slides.heading: Characteristics of PHC
bullets: Community-based
Accessible (within 3–5 km, within 30 minutes)
Sustainable
Affordable (low cost)
Self-reliance
Available

terms.definition: Patient is healthy — health education and immunization (health promotion & illness prevention).
High-risk individuals — early diagnosis, screening and treatment to prevent complications.
Post-treatment — rehabilitation and palliative care to limit disability and restore function.

slides.heading: Micronutrients & Deficiencies
bullets: Vitamin A (Retinol) deficiency → Bitot's spots, corneal clouding, xerophthalmia, night blindness.
Food Fortification (Sangkap Pinoy) targets micronutrients — given April & October.
Iron → Iron Deficiency Anemia; best taken on an empty stomach (acidic) with orange juice/calamansi.
Iodine deficiency → goiter and mental retardation (given once/year).

slides.heading: Immunization — EPI
bullets: Expanded Program on Immunization → DOH National Immunization Program (NIP).
PD 996 (1976): free vaccines for children below 8 years old.
RA 10152 (2011): mandatory immunization for children below 5 years old.
Pentavalent (5-in-1): Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B + HiB (prevents meningitis).
National Immunization Day: Wednesday; BHS monthly; GIDA quarterly.

slides.heading: Cold Chain
bullets: All vaccines are sensitive to heat.
Most heat-sensitive (Freezer −15°C to −25°C): Varicella, OPV, MMR.
Body of refrigerator (+2°C to +8°C): BCG, Hepa B, Pentavalent, PCV, Rota, IPV, TT/TD.
Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM): if the inner square is LIGHTER than the circle — OK to give.

slides.heading: Key Vaccine Notes
bullets: BCG: contraindicated in AIDS, leukemia, chemotherapy; clean site with water only; Koch's phenomenon.
Pentavalent: fever → paracetamol; seizure/convulsion (from pertussis) within 3 days → withhold Penta 2 & 3.
OPV: live attenuated, on the tongue; if vomits within 30 min, repeat the dose.
MMR: live attenuated; fever → paracetamol, rashes → keep dry.

slides.heading: Sanitation — Water Facility Levels
rows: Point source — protected/deep well, developed spring; >250 m; rural.
Communal faucet / stand posts; 1 per 4–5 households.
Individual household connection; waterworks system; cleanest.

slides.heading: Sanitation — Toilet Facility Levels
rows: Pour-flush / water-sealed toilet with septic tank.
Level 2 + sewerage system & treatment plant; cleanest.

slides.heading: Food Safety (4 Rights) & Codes
bullets: Right Source (fresh), Right Preparation (wash), Right Cooking (70°C), Right Storage (cool 10°C / warm 60°C).
Room temperature: maximum of 2 hours.
PD 856 — Sanitation Code of the Philippines; PD 825 — Garbage Disposal Act.
Establishment: owner needs a sanitary permit; food handlers need a health certificate.

terms.definition: Greater than the normal number of cases in an area within a short period.

slides.heading: Vital Statistics
rows: Natural increase — total births / total population × 1000
Natural decrease — total deaths / total population × 1000
Index of prenatal care — deaths due to pregnancy / live births × 1000
Index of health status — deaths >28 d to <1 yr / live births × 1000
Acute disease (<6 mo) — new cases / total population × 1000
Chronic disease (>6 mo) — old + new cases / persons examined × 100
Best index of community health — deaths >50 yo / total deaths × 100

slides.heading: Maternal & Child Health
bullets: Prenatal visits: 8 (WHO) / 4 (DOH); Sentrong Sigla = quality assurance program.
BEmOC: oxytocin, antibiotic, anticonvulsant (MgSO4 for pre-eclampsia), steroids, assisted delivery, manual placenta removal.
CEmOC: BEmOC + blood transfusion & cesarean section.
AMTSL (3rd stage of labor): IM oxytocin → controlled cord traction → uterine massage.

slides.heading: Essential Newborn Care (Unang Yakap)
bullets: Time-bound: dry infant immediately → early skin-to-skin → delayed cord clamping (1–3 min) → breastfeeding (exclusive 6 months).
Non-time-bound: Hepatitis B, Vitamin K, erythromycin eye ointment, anthropometric measurement, APGAR (1 & 5 min).
Unnecessary/avoid: routine suctioning, slapping/heel stimulation, footprinting, milking the cord, immediate bathing, antiseptic on the stump.
Newborn screening detects genetic disorders to prevent mental retardation and premature death.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: PHC: Alma Ata 1978; LOI 949; vision "Health in the hands of the people."
Pillars: active participation (most important), linkages, appropriate technology, support.
Master the EPI schedule, cold chain, and wastage factors.
MCH essentials: TT schedule, BEmOC/CEmOC, and Unang Yakap (EINC).
